topIssues.title: kona-node: verify delegated derivation parity against op-node
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#545.

The tracker's completion criteria include verification work that no fix PR covers. This issue tracks it so the parity claim rests on exercised behavior, not only on unit tests in the three core fixes (#23675, #23676, #23677).

Scope:
- Verify safe and finalized progress by block hash and ancestry, comparing CL and EL labels, with unsafe production paused.
- Exercise source-ahead catch-up and an EL answering SYNCING followed by VALID, including unchanged-target retries and eventual recovery.
- Exercise stale-source finalized references and confirm finalized never moves backward and conflicting hashes are not accepted.
- Run the follow-source acceptance cases against Kona, or explicitly retain and link the remaining gaps: #22272, #22273, #22274.
- Record results on #545 and tick the corresponding completion checkboxes.

topIssues.title: kona-client: the library cannot be built for a no_std target
topIssues.author: yoshidan
topIssues.body:
`kona-client`'s library side — `fpvm_evm`, `interop`, `single` — never references `kona_std_fpvm`; only the two binary sources, `src/kona.rs` and `src/kona_interop.rs`, do. But `kona-std-fpvm` and `kona-std-fpvm-proc` are declared unconditionally in `[dependencies]`, so cargo builds them for the library too. `kona-std-fpvm` reads the preimage oracle over file descriptors (`std::fs::File`, `std::os::fd`) and carries no `#![no_std]`, so a consumer that wants only the library cannot build for a `no_std` target:

```
error: `std` is required by `kona_std_fpvm` because it does not declare `#![no_std]`
```

No feature avoids it today: `client-tracing`, the only one, enables `kona-std-fpvm/tracing`.

We hit this building an Intel SGX enclave. The OP Stack light client in [datachainlab/optimism-elc](https://github.com/datachainlab/optimism-elc) uses `kona_client::fpvm_evm::FpvmOpEvmFactory`, and the enclave is built for a custom `x86_64-unknown-unknown-sgx` target with `-Z build-std=core,alloc`, where no `std` exists at all.

`kona-client` is also absent from `no_std_packages` in `rust/justfile`, so `just check-no-std` does not cover it.

### Proposal

Move both dependencies behind a new `fpvm` feature, gate the two `[[bin]]` targets on it with `required-features`, and have `client-tracing` enable it. `default` still enables `client-tracing`, so the ordinary build is unchanged; only a consumer that opts out with `default-features = false` sees a difference. Adding `kona-client` to `no_std_packages` would keep it from regressing.

We have this working against `kona-client/v1.9.0` and are glad to open the PR if the approach looks reasonable.

topPRs.title: Fix translation drift
topPRs.author: mintlify
topPRs.body:
## Summary
Adds a full Korean (`ko`) translation of all English MDX and markdown docs, plus a Korean language section in the navigation.

## Changes
- Added 484 translated files under `ko/`, mirroring the source tree. This includes snippets, which are now under `ko/snippets/`. Korean pages import from `/ko/snippets/...`; `.jsx` snippets stay shared.
- Restructured `docs.json` navigation into `languages`. `en` keeps the existing tabs. `ko` mirrors them with `ko/`-prefixed pages and translated tab and group names.
- Rewrote internal links to `/ko/...`. Links that relied on English redirects now point straight to the final targets.
- `mint validate` and `mint broken-links` both pass.

## Notes
- Translated headings change auto-generated anchor IDs. Some `#anchor` fragments may no longer land on the right section, but the links still open the correct page.
- Generated snippets under `ko/snippets/generated/` need to be updated by hand when the English ones are regenerated.

topPRs.title: ci: pilot RWX with shared routing and shadow tests
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
PR validation currently rebuilds op-reth in CircleCI and lacks executed RWX parity evidence. This pilot runs the complete op-reth release producer and its three associated checks alongside shared routing, Go lint/Rust formatting, Go rollup tests and four standard-contract configurations. CircleCI continues to own the required gates.

The op-reth shadow builds both release binaries, runs every selected `reth-optimism-node` test through a nextest archive, generates fresh compact vectors with pinned develop and reads them with the PR binary, and regenerates both superchain snapshots. It uses shared dependency downloads, content caching, separate native tool caches for Cargo targets and sccache, parallel codec compilers, pinned tools and SHA-bound artifacts. Checksum-matching superchain bundles retain their timestamps. Release, integration and codec consumers mount artifacts directly instead of inheriting compiler-cache layers. Every verdict and vector generation executes freshly.

Validation:

- At `0b7935e7339726c1b1166be6372fbf057fb251dd`, [native op-reth CI](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/0d4989f8fc044b48888ba7cdda9e9b2a) passed all four workloads in **6m20s**. All 50 runnable integration cases passed; one explicitly ignored case remained in discovery. Original JUnit identities and outcomes matched [CircleCI job 5625881](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5625881) exactly. All four RWX status checks are green at this head.
- Direct artifact mounts removed both compiler-cache trees from the codec verifier. Its measured preparation fell from 171s at `99ccc76a` to 2s at this head, followed by fresh execution in 5s. The final consumer received a 622 MiB binary artifact and two small vector/provenance artifacts, and its metadata confirmed the PR checkout. Both observations are single samples, with different runner-local layer states.
- Before the bundle/artifact optimizations, the complete RWX run at `d2b90241` took 13m10s initially and [5m58s with warm tool caches](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/2c7e09f8233541869ff6fa8771b3d372). A [forced target-cache probe](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/8545eb684d094e13abc4e91fdab645fe) after bundle retention executed snapshot preparation in 7s, with six Rust sccache hits and zero misses; fresh regeneration still ran for 24s.
- An [empty-target probe](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/8552f40db3314cf282583313806e0be6) produced 263 Rust hits and zero misses in 36s. An [identical-input release rerun](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/be0b0006cd5044c88739ec46cd81f2d6) reused the compiler content cache and finished the release path in 8s, including fresh binary verification. A separate warm release rebuild recorded 27 Rust hits and no misses but still spent 236s compiling/linking; content reuse and incremental reuse have different benefits.
- An [intentional CLI-only test fault](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/add6576e7432497a8a1e3f85a40a8313) failed the task and run, preserved nextest's exit 100, and retained original JUnit and partial coverage. Committed Rust tests were unchanged.
- 22 cache/provenance/report regression tests, 35 routing scenarios, shell checks and RWX configuration validation passed. The final native artifact consumers inherited no op-reth compiler caches; only snapshot regeneration retained Cargo targets.

Implementation coverage is **10/86 expanded PR jobs, about 12%**. The [parity checklist](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/rwx-ci-pilot/docs/ai/rwx-parity-todos.md) and [measurements](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/rwx-ci-pilot/docs/ai/rwx-migration.md#first-hosted-measurements) track representative Rust source-change probes, repeated actual-resource timings and billed usage, smaller tool/compiler layers, and a protected cache-rebuild policy before promotion. Whole-run duration, compiler phases and billed cost remain separate measurements; declared resource classes do not prove identical hardware. Full Go/acceptance producers and consumers, remaining Rust/contracts, routing and identity cutover remain open.

Earlier Go/contract comparisons at `587b4c3a` still need authoritative CircleCI discovery, 178 contract skip reasons and fresh evidence for 17 cached Go cases. Schedules, publishing and privileged writer ownership remain with CircleCI. The cache-only RWX vault has no production credentials and restricted pilot/develop writers; remove the temporary pilot grant and evict pilot cache entries before promotion.

This single draft PR replaces #23141, #23142, #23144 and #23148 and remains the ongoing home for the pilot.

**Description**

Adds `ComplianceModule` so deposits and withdrawals can wait for policy clearance, then complete on their original terms. The module holds deferred value, and a replaceable policy decides whether it can move.

The module uses its own `ProxyAdmin` outside OPCM to separate custody upgrade authority from policy management. The policy implementation and broader integration coverage follow separately.

**Metadata**

- Closes ethereum-optimism/optimism-private#742

topPRs.title: op-deployer!: run live apply and bootstrap on forge by default
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Stack 2/7, merge in order: #23663 → #23664 → #23665 → #23666 → #23667 → #23668 → #23669. The whole change, with green CI, is #23647.

The Go script host needs EVM hooks that only op-geth has, so it blocks the move to upstream go-ethereum (#20266). op-deployer already had an opt-in forge path for live deployments. This PR makes that path dependable and the default for live `apply` and `bootstrap`. Genesis deployments, the L2 genesis, `prepare` and `continue` still run on the Go script host; later PRs of the stack move them.

**Effect on users**

- Live `apply` and `bootstrap` run on forge. `--use-forge=false` still runs them on the Go script host, until #23308 removes the flag. `--forge-slow-broadcast` is removed: every broadcast sends one transaction at a time.
- As txmgr did, each transaction gets the node's gas estimate just before forge sends it, a tip of at least 1 gwei, and a fee cap of twice the base fee (at least 1 gwei) plus the tip. Unlike txmgr, forge does not bump the fee of, or resubmit, a stuck transaction.
- forge gets the deployer key in a temporary encrypted keystore that only the user can read, never on its command line.
- op-deployer never compiles. It refuses a contracts bundle whose scripts have no `runWithBytes` entrypoint, and it stops forge as soon as forge starts to compile. So a live deployment needs the contracts release of the same op-deployer release: an `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier release is refused (`tag://` locators were already rejected). The default, `embedded`, works, and `--use-forge=false` keeps the Go script host until #23308.
- A contracts bundle is a forge project, so op-deployer does not trust its `foundry.toml`: scripts run without FFI, with file access only to the artifacts, and forge inherits only the environment variables that it needs (`verify-contract` keeps the full environment, for its API key). Each forge script loads every artifact of the project, about 1.3 GB, so forge runs take one of `GOMAXPROCS/2` slots per host.
- forge's output goes to stderr. A failed script reports its revert reason.
- The artifacts-locators page no longer lists `tag://` locators, which op-deployer already rejects. The manual Sepolia test script no longer offers the Go script host as its default engine.
- The forge download detects musl, uses `--cache-dir`, and gives a clear error without network access. The Windows release binaries are no longer built.

**Reasons the diff does not show**

- Each broadcast sends one transaction at a time: without `--slow`, forge waited forever when a node dropped one of several transactions that it sent at once.
- forge runs are not `--offline`: offline, forge requires every solc version of the cache installed even when it compiles nothing. A compile watcher enforces "never compile" instead.
- Every forge run uses its own copy of the compile cache and its own broadcast directory, so that concurrent runs (devstack) do not interfere.
- Bundle builds (Docker, melange, `just forge-build`) run one `forge script` to warm the script cache, and fail when a second run would compile: a single script's compile can choose other solc versions than the project build.
- CI jobs that run op-deployer from the checkout now check out the contracts `lib/` submodules: forge reads the sources to check its compile cache.
- sysgo waits for the L1 transaction index before it deploys chains: geth rejects receipt queries until its first indexing pass, and forge gives up after a few quick retries.
- The test `RetryProxy` gives a client error (4xx, not 429) to the client at once: forge calls methods such as `anvil_nodeInfo` that a proxyd endpoint answers with 403, and the retries held each call for about 40 s.
- The `forge` package tests run in CI only after #23643, which removes the package from the CI exclusion list.

**Reviews**

go-code-reviewer on the transitional code of this PR and the next two. Fixed: the BREAKING CHANGE text named `tag://` instead of `https://`/`file://` bundles, and `--use-forge=false` had no test (a live subtest now covers it).

**Known limits, not fixed here**

Live deploys could keep txmgr by simulating on an anvil fork and replaying, as `continue` does (#23306); the #23300 plan chose `forge script --broadcast`. The RPC URL stays on the command line of forge, which has no environment binding for it. A crash during a broadcast can leave the encrypted keystore and its password file in a directory that only the user can read (forge refuses a password pipe). A forge binary in the cache directory is trusted by its version.

Closes #23302.

BREAKING CHANGE: `op-deployer apply` and `op-deployer bootstrap` run on forge by default; `--use-forge=false` runs them on the Go script host until a later release removes it. `--forge-slow-broadcast` is removed. An `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier contracts release is refused for live `apply` and `bootstrap`; use `embedded`, or `--use-forge=false` until the Go script host is removed. Go callers replace `ApplyPipelineOpts.UseForge`, `ForgeSlowBroadcast` and `PrivateKey` with `UseScriptHost` (zero value: forge) and `DeployerPrivateKey`; `pipeline.Env`'s `ForgeClient`, `UseForge`, `L1RPCUrl` and `PrivateKey` with `Forge`; and bootstrap's `UseForge` and `ForgeSlowBroadcast` with `UseScriptHost`. `forge.ScriptCaller` returns `(output, error)` without the recompiled flag, and `forge.Client.SlowBroadcast` is removed. The Windows release binaries are no longer built.

topPRs.title: kona-gossip,kona-rpc!: Enforce peer, address and subnet blocks on inbound and existing connections
topPRs.author: aakoshh
topPRs.body:
### What

kona-node now enforces the operator's peer, address and subnet blocks, and score bans, on inbound connections and on connections that are already open, not only on its own dials. `opp2p_connectPeer` and `opp2p_disconnectPeer` now wait for the result and report why a connection fails.

### Why

Before this PR, a block only stopped kona's own dials. A blocked peer, or a peer at a blocked address, could still dial in, and an open connection stayed open after its peer was blocked. A score ban disconnected the peer, but nothing kept it from reconnecting at once.

For operators:
- **Blocks** (`opp2p_blockPeer`, `opp2p_blockAddr`, `opp2p_blockSubnet`) refuse inbound connections, by address before the handshake, and close existing connections in both directions. They also apply to protected and static peers. op-node, by contrast, leaves open connections in place. A block that covers a static peer is logged as a warning.
- **Score bans** (`--p2p.ban.peers`) refuse the peer in both directions until the ban expires. As in op-node, `opp2p_unblockPeer` lifts a ban, and bans aren't listed by `opp2p_listBlockedPeers`.
- **`opp2p_connectPeer`** used to fail at once with "Peer not connected" for any peer, because its poll never retried. It now waits up to 30 seconds for the connection, as op-node does, fails at once with the gate's reason for a blocked or banned peer, and returns the dial's error when the dial fails. **`opp2p_disconnectPeer`** waits for the connections to close. Both return only once the P2P RPC's state shows the change, so an `opp2p_peers` call right after lists it. The devstack's `connectL2CLPeers` relies on that.
- **RPC errors:** these two methods' failures now use code `-32000` with the reason, as op-node's do, where they used `-32602` (invalid params) with "Peer not connected" or "Peers are still connected". An address that names no peer, or has nothing to dial before its `/p2p/<peer id>`, is still `-32602`, with a message saying which.
- **`opp2p_peers`** reports `latency` in nanoseconds, as op-node does. It was in whole seconds, so always `0`.
- **The `payload_by_number` sync protocol is no longer served.** op-node retired both its client and its server. kona's stub read each request without a size limit or timeout, so a peer could stream bytes into the node until it ran out of memory.
- **Metrics:** `kona_node_gossip_inbound_connections_refused` is new, by `reason`. `kona_node_dial_peer_error{type="already_connected"}` now counts less, since `opp2p_connectPeer` to a connected peer no longer dials.
- **Logs:** peers connecting and disconnecting are logged at debug, no longer at info and warn. A gossip listener that closes while the node runs is logged as an error.
- **The P2P RPC** answers from gossip state up to a second old. What a command changes shows at once, and so do connection, identify, subscription and address changes. If the network actor doesn't publish fresher state within two seconds, a call answers from the last state.

Closes #23715. Closes #23701.

### How

- **The blocks live in `gate::Behaviour`, a `NetworkBehaviour`,** the first field of the gossip `Behaviour`. The swarm asks its behaviours about a connection in `handle_pending_inbound_connection`, before the handshake, and in `handle_established_*_connection`, once the peer ID is known. These are the only points where a connection can be refused. By the time the driver sees `ConnectionEstablished`, gossipsub has already queued its subscriptions, so the driver could only close the connection again. Being the first field means the gate is asked before gossipsub, identify and ping.
- **`ConnectionGater` keeps only the dial bookkeeping,** and checks the gate it is given. The gater's write-only `connectedness` map is gone (#23701).
- **The RPC's gossip snapshot is built on demand.** The network actor used to rebuild it after every step: for each gossip message, ping and identify event. It now publishes after each command, and when a reader asks for one fresher than the reader's `max_age`, through a refresh channel with room for one request, so readers that ask at the same time share one build. It also publishes when the swarm reports a change the snapshot shows.
- **`ConnectPeer` and `DisconnectPeer` carry a reply,** which the driver answers from the swarm event that settles the outcome. `ConnectPeer` carries a `PeerAddr`, so the RPC parses the address once. A refusal by the gate, before the dial or once the connection is established, comes back typed, as `ConnectPeerError::Refused`.
- **`GossipDriver::start` returns a `PeerAddr`,** which always ends in the node's peer ID.
- **The devstack's `TestP2PPeers`** expected a blocked peer to stay connected, as in op-node. On kona nodes, it now waits for the connection to close, and reconnects the peer after unblocking it.

### Caveats

- A peer refused by its peer ID still completes the Noise handshake, since the ID is only known after it. op-node's `InterceptSecured` works the same way. Address and subnet blocks refuse before the handshake.
- A static peer given by a DNS name can't be matched against an address block until it is connected, so the warning about blocking it may not appear.
- Blocks and bans don't survive a restart (#23768).
- Scores and ping latencies in RPC answers can be up to a second old, since they change without an event.
- A gossip listener that closes while the node runs is logged, but the node keeps running without it (#23793).
- op-node versions that still run the sync request client get "protocol not supported" from kona now, and may score it down. That client has been off by default since #18088, and was removed in op-node v1.19.1.
- The `opp2p_*` methods are served to anyone who can reach the RPC port, which listens on `0.0.0.0` by default, as in op-node. Blocks are stronger now, so `opp2p_blockSubnet 0.0.0.0/0` cuts the node off from every peer (#23798).
- The gossip peerstore keeps every peer that ever completed identify. This PR also stops removing a banned peer's entry, for parity with op-node (#23800).

### Alternatives

- **The blocklist as shared state in the driver** (`Arc<RwLock>`): rejected, because the driver only sees a connection after it is established, and can't refuse it before.
- **Bounding the sync stub instead of removing it:** done first, in its own commit (read exactly the 8-byte request, with op-node's 10-second deadline), then removed, since op-node no longer uses the protocol.
- **Dialing an unblocked static peer at once:** rejected. `opp2p_connectPeer` covers the urgent case, and the driver would have needed another way to schedule its checks. The peer is dialed at the next check, within a minute.
- **Listing score bans in `opp2p_listBlockedPeers`:** rejected, for parity with op-node, and because a tool that copies blocks between nodes would turn temporary bans into permanent blocks. Making bans visible is #23796.

- **Dropping `test_sync_request_protocol_is_unsupported` once the protocol was gone,** as a review suggested: kept, so that a peer asking for the protocol is shown to get "protocol not supported", rather than a stream kona never answers.

### Potential follow-ups

- Split `kona-gossip/src/driver.rs`, now about 2,000 lines, into a module by concern, as a pure move.
- Move the JSON-RPC wire types (`PeerInfo`, `PeerDump`, ...) from `kona-gossip` to `kona-rpc`, or to an RPC-types crate.
- Make `GossipDriver` generic over its message handler. Today it knows OP payload types, the v1–v4 block topics and the signer rotation, and takes the chain ID from the block handler's rollup config.
- `NetworkActor::step` is hard to read and to test as one `select!`. The `next`/`handle` split proposed in #23534 and #23580 would help, for example for #23793.
- Filed: #23793 (stop the node when the gossip listener closes), #23796 (show score bans over the RPC, and the misleading `banned*` field names), #23797 (late blocks from the previous signer are rejected at a signer rotation), #23798 (don't serve the P2P control methods to anyone who can reach the RPC port), #23800 (prune disconnected peers from the peerstore), #23768 (keep blocks and bans across restarts, now with a startup warning about blocked static peers).

BREAKING CHANGE: Rust users of `kona-gossip` and `kona-rpc` need to update their code; the node's command-line flags and RPC methods don't change.
- The sync request/response protocol is gone, with `Behaviour::sync_req_resp`, `GossipDriverBuilderError::{SetupSyncReqRespError, SyncReqRespAlreadyAccepted}` and `Event::Stream`.
- `GossipDriver`'s `swarm`, `addr`, `handler` and `peerstore` fields are private, and `behaviour_mut` is gone. Use `addr()`, `handler()`, `peer_addr()`, `connected_peers()` (now the peer IDs, not a count), and the driver's `block_*`, `unblock_*` and `list_blocked_*` methods.
- `ConnectionGater`'s blocklist and `connectedness` fields, and the `ConnectionGate` trait's block, list and `connectedness` methods, are gone; `ConnectionGate::can_dial` takes the `gate::Behaviour`.
- `GossipDriver::start` returns a `PeerAddr`; `dial_peer` and `dial_multiaddr` return a `Result`.
- `GossipCommand::ConnectPeer` carries a `PeerAddr` named `peer` and a reply sender, and `DisconnectPeer` a reply sender. `GossipDriver::connect_peer` takes a `PeerAddr`.
- `NetworkActorError::DriverStartup` is gone; nothing returned it.
- `GossipQueryHandle::new` takes the refresh sender, and `GossipQueryHandle::snapshot` is async and takes the oldest snapshot age the caller accepts. `GossipState::pings` is a field.
